question: Should OpenClaw accept Android device-control, ADB-style access, or dynamic Android code execution in core, and what command-policy, permission, and sandbox boundary should govern it?
rationale: The remaining requested tools can control a phone, read sensitive state, and potentially execute arbitrary code, so automation cannot choose the acceptable product and security boundary.

options.title: Narrow safe commands first
options.body: Approve only explicit Android device-control commands that have Android permission UX, gateway allowlist policy, and focused tests; defer ADB and arbitrary Kotlin execution.

options.title: Route execution through node-host/plugin APIs
options.body: Keep high-power ADB and dynamic execution out of the Android app and require an existing or newly approved node-host/plugin-tool path with exec approvals and policy controls.

options.title: Defer Android execution work
options.body: Keep this umbrella open for discussion but do not accept more Android control or execution surface until a maintainer-owned security design exists.

recommendation.title: Narrow safe commands first
recommendation.body: Approve only explicit Android device-control commands that have Android permission UX, gateway allowlist policy, and focused tests; defer ADB and arbitrary Kotlin execution.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus supplied the clearest prior product-direction comment on Android session behavior and landed the related Android node work.
